Keys led Zheng Qinwen 5-0 in the final set of their third-round match before collapsing in the final set as she lost 1-6, 7-6 (3), 7-5. “I think she started playing better; I started playing poorly,” Keys said. “Then I felt like I couldn’t play tennis any more, and it just was – it just felt like it was a much bigger deal than just playing a tennis match all of a sudden.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenZheng Qinwen set up a last-16 match against Iga Swiatek after fighting back to beat Madison Keys in three sets.Photograph: Heather Khalifa/APKeys,the 2025 Australian Open champion, said she believes a result like this had been coming for some time and will force her to address certain issues she has been dealing with. “I just feel like I’ve been struggling for a while now and I feel like I was able to kind of play through it for a bit,” she said. “I’m sure everyone could kind of see that I was struggling a little bit, but inside it felt probably even bigger than that. Some weeks are easier than others, and this week is obviously one of the harder ones just because you care so much. Yeah, I’m going to have to make some changes.”For Zheng, however, this was an enormous win. Havingwon the Olympic gold medaland reached the top 10 in 2024, the Chinese player has fallen down the rankings since her return from elbow surgery and the 23-year-old was forced to come through qualifying here just to compete in the main draw.“Tennis sometimes feels like a rollercoaster,” Zheng said. “You see many times that people have a match point, but at the end [their opponent] makes a comeback. Like today was just happening. So this also gives me a lesson that in a tennis match you always have to be there. It doesn’t matter if you are winning or losing, you have a match point or you don’t have a match point – you just need to be concentrated for every single point as long as you can.”Amanda Anisimova, whose incredible breakthrough summer of 2025 included runners-up finishes at Wimbledon and the US Open alongside a career-high ranking of No 3, will fall out of the top 10 after tamely losing 6-2, 7-5 to the 24th seed Anastasia Potapova. Iga Swiatek, meanwhile, brilliantly saved three set points in her second set before working her way to a tough 7-6 (3), 7-6 (3) win over Marie Bouzkova. Swiatek faces Zheng in the fourth round on Sunday.Explore more on these topicsUS Open Tennis 2026US Open tennisTennisUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Katie Taylor bows out from boxing as undisputed champion after dominating Flora Pili | Katie Taylor | The Guardian
description: Irish fans at Croke Park saluted their retiring hero as Katie Taylor overwhelmed Flora Pili, as reflected in scorecards that read 110-90, 110-90 and 98-91
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Irish fans at Croke Park saluted their retiring hero as Katie Taylor overwhelmed Flora Pili, as reflected in scorecards that read 110-90, 110-90 and 98-91
Content: Katie Taylor beams in the Croke Park ring after what she describes as ‘a dream end to a dream career’.Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKatie Taylor beams in the Croke Park ring after what she describes as ‘a dream end to a dream career’.Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty ImagesKatie TaylorKatie Taylor bows out from boxing as undisputed champion after dominating Flora PiliIrish fans dazzled by showcase of skills in huge points winScorecards read 110-90, 110-90 and 98-91 in her favourGuardian sportand agenciesSat 5 Sep 2026 18.18 EDTLast modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 18.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKatie Taylor signed off her storied career in style by outclassing Flora Pili on points as an 80,000 crowd at Croke Park celebrated her fairytale farewell.With the gaze ofIrelandupon her, the country’s great became a three-time undisputed world champion by overwhelming the previously unbeaten Frenchwoman 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 on the scorecards.Boxer Thomas Carty falls out of ring after 92 seconds in bizarre no-contestRead moreTaylor dominated through her hand speed and movement and never looked in danger as she added the vacant WBC title to her WBO, WBA and IBF belts to begin the party at GAA headquarters.As the final seconds before retirement approached, the Olympic gold medallist ended the 10th round by trading with Pili against the ropes knowing victory was assured.The victory completed a remarkable journey for Taylor, who began boxing at a time when girls were barred from amateur competition in Ireland and sometimes entered bouts simply as “K Taylor”.She went on to win Olympic lightweight gold at London 2012, when women’s boxing made its Games debut, before turning professional four years later.Taylor finishes her professional career with 26 victories and one defeat, having won world titles at lightweight and super-lightweight.Her farewell also brought top-level boxing back to Croke Park for the first time since Muhammad Ali defeated Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972.View image in fullscreenKatie Taylor’s speed and ringcraft told from first bell to last as she left Flora Pili well outclassed.Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty ImagesFollowing the fight, she placed her gloves in the centre of the ring to mark her retirement, while her team assisted her in assembling her belts around them.Addressing the buoyant crowd, she said: “Croke Park! We did it,” said ‌Taylor as she saluted the crowd. “I don’t know of any other country that ​would sell 80,000 tickets.”She later added: “The people of Ireland gave me a dream end to a dream career. Nothing can top this.”Explore more on these topicsKatie TaylorBoxingIrelandnewsShareReuse this content

title: High-flying Hull stay unbeaten by holding off Aston Villa in stalemate | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Aston Villa remain without a win while Hull are still unbeaten after a 0-0 draw at MKM Stadium
Author: Ross Heppenstall
Headline: Aston Villa remain without a win while Hull are still unbeaten after a 0-0 draw at MKM Stadium
Content: Oli McBurnie taking on three Aston Villa defenders by himself epitomised Hull’s spirit.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenOli McBurnie taking on three Aston Villa defenders by himself epitomised Hull’s spirit.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/ReutersPremier LeagueHigh-flying Hull stay unbeaten by holding off Aston Villa in stalemateRoss Heppenstallat the MKM StadiumSat 5 Sep 2026 14.28 EDTLast modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 16.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt’s never dull in Hull, as the saying goes in these parts, and after just three games thePremier Leagueis proving to be quite some ride for Hull City supporters.Having embarrassed Manchester United hereon the opening day andwon at Coventry last weekend, this deserved point and third successive clean sheet merely reinforced Sergej Jakirovic’s belief that his men can beat the drop.Hull City 0-0 Aston Villa: Premier League – as it happenedRead moreYou have to go back to Bolton’s excellent start in 2001-02 to find a promoted side who began the season with three straight victories. The Tigers failed to emulate Sam Allardyce’s team, but they came closest to a winner as the Algeria winger Mohamed Belloumi hit the crossbar with a stunning second-half shot before the substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho and Oli McBurnie threatened late on.“We could have won, but they also had a few chances in the second half,” said Jakirovic, who signed a two-year contract extension on Friday. “We won’t be ungrateful for seven points after three games and another clean sheet. It’s a great result for us and we showed we can compete at this level.”ForAston Villa, it was another largely impotent display which saw them fail to score for the third match running as the captain, John McGinn, and Emiliano Buendía spurned decent second-half opportunities.Villa failed to manage a shot on target whenbeing hammered 4-0 at Brightonandlosing 1-0 at home to Arsenal; here they managed just one, a tame shot by George Hemmings early on.Unai Emery chose to take the positives from Villa’s displayas he patiently rebuilds the clubafter a summer of major upheaval which saw a number of key players leave and 10 new faces arrive.View image in fullscreenGeorge Hemmings had Aston Villa’s first shot on target of the Premier League season, 13 minutes into their third game.Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters“The result is not enough, but I think we deserved more,” he said. “We weren’t clinical but of course to win matches, you need goals. We created chances today to score and we must improve but we are rebuilding.”Ambition pulsed loudly at a sold-out MKM Stadium before kick-off as a huge amber banner inscribed with the words “One family, one dream” was paraded on the pitch. It said much for the togethernessthat Jakirovic has fashioned within his squadand the connection with the club’s supporters during a remarkable few months in the Tigers’ history.Desire was visible and audible in the stands and on the pitch, but Villa almost led inside the second minute when Nicolas Jackson headed Ian Maatsen’s teasing left-wing cross wastefully wide.Hull were unfazed and Belloumi beat Ross Barkley twice, including with a delightful nutmeg, before breaking clear down the right flank. His low cross was cleared, but it hinted at the possibilities on offer for the hosts.In the 13th minute, Villa finally fashioned their only effort on target this season as Hemmings’s low shot was comfortably saved by Konstantinos Tzolakis.If Villa could not see off a promoted side widely tipped for an immediate relegation this season, could they really consider themselves ready to start climbing the table? A neat passing sequence should have brought a Villa goal in the 50th minute but McGinn could only lift the ball harmlessly over Tzolakis’s crossbar from less than 12 yards out.Three minutes later, Villa went even closer as Hemmings outstripped the Hull captain, Lewie Coyle, down the left flank and showed intelligence to pick out Buendía with a neat cut-back. Buendía should have buried the chance but he blazed wildly over, much to his disgust.In the 65th minute, Hull went agonisingly close to scoring when Belloumi collected possession from a short corner and curled a stunning left-foot shot against the bar. There was a resilience to the hosts, and the collective desirethat carried them to promotion last seasonwill be needed over the next 35 games if they are to defy the odds and beat the drop.It was evident again late on when the Hull substitute Lucas Herrington –on his 19th birthday– produced a vital block to repel Tyrone Mings’s shot. Cho’s close-range effort was then repelledby Zion Suzukibefore McBurnie failed to properly connect with Giles’s cross as Hull looked likeliest to nick a late winner.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueHull CityAston Villamatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Pierre Gasly takes shock pole for F1 Italian GP as Alpine stun big guns | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: Alpine’s Pierre Gasly took the first pole position of his nine-year F1 career at the Italian GP, ahead of British driver George Russell
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Alpine’s Pierre Gasly took the first pole position of his nine-year F1 career at the Italian GP, ahead of British driver George Russell
Content: Pierre Gasly celebrates his pole at Monza.Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/ReutersView image in fullscreenPierre Gasly celebrates his pole at Monza.Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/ReutersFormula One 2026Pierre Gasly takes shock pole for F1 Italian GP as Alpine stun big gunsLandmark for Frenchman at his 190th meetingRussell on front row, Hamilton fifth on gridGiles Richardsat MonzaSat 5 Sep 2026 11.20 EDTLast modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 14.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePierre Gasly has run the gamut from bitter disappointment to absolute elation in the past two days, and there is surely no better pick-me-up than claiming an extraordinary firstFormula Onepole position at the Italian Grand Prix at Monza, one of the sport’s greatest venues.What it meant to the Frenchman was clear. “Nine years I’ve been in Formula One, I’m trying to give my best every single weekend. It’s not every time we get a car to fight for pole position,” he said. “Today was the case. I’m really happy, really proud to have seized this chance and made it work. It was a hell of a lap.”Lewis Hamilton calls on Ferrari to put full weight behind F1 title challengeRead moreOn Thursday, Gasly and Alpine were told his third place at the Monaco Grand Prix had been overturned by the FIA’s international court of appeal (ICA), after McLaren and Red Bull had taken the case there. Gasly had been stripped of his podium and it hurt; indeed led to Alpine’s executive adviser, Flavio Briatore, making extraordinary allegations of pro-McLaren bias by one of the ICA judges.The allegations were addressed by the ICA on Saturday but the response Gasly would have wanted most was on track, and he and Alpine delivered to perfection. Steve Nielsen, the Alpine managing director, perhaps best expressed what it meant. “We were all on the floor. It’s from being really down to being on top of the world in just two days,” he said. “Pierre is a class act: if you give him the machine, he will deliver.”The 30-year-old Frenchman, who lives nearby in Milan, has finally taken the top spot at his 190th meeting, during his ninth full season in F1. They have waited a long time in France too, with 29 years passing since Jean Alesi was the last Frenchman to take pole at Monza. With pleasing symmetry, he was driving for Benetton, the Enstone-based team that would ultimately become Alpine.Quick GuideItalian F1 GP qualifying resultsShow1Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine1:21.8762George Russell🇬🇧Mercedes1:21.846†3Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren1:21.9664Charles Leclerc🇲🇨Ferrari1:22.0045Lewis Hamilton🇬🇧Ferrari1:22.0116Max Verstappen🇳🇱Red Bull1:22.070*7Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes1:22.0938Franco Colapinto🇦🇷Alpine1:22.2209Lando Norris🇬🇧McLaren1:22.25610Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls1:22.286Q2 eliminations11Gabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷Audi1:22.51712Oliver Bearman🇬🇧Haas1:22.75613Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi1:22.779*14Liam Lawson🇫🇷Red Bull1:22.82115Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams1:23.45316Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas1:23.454Q1 eliminations17Yuki Tsunoda🇯🇵Racing Bulls1:23.755*18Alexander Albon🇹🇭Williams1:24.35619Valtteri Bottas🇫🇮Cadillac1:24.36420Sergio Pérez🇲🇽Cadillac1:24.59521Fernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston Martin1:25.15022Lance Stroll🇨🇦Aston Martin1:25.22† Piastri given a three-place grid penalty for impeding Lawson. *Antonelli, Lawson and Albon all relegated to the back of the grid for taking new power unit elementsWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.On a high-speed blast at the Autodromo Nazionale Monza the margins are tiny, and finding the very limit vital; indeed Gasly’s margin over the second-placed Mercedes of George Russell was just six-hundredths of a second. Gasly was on a knife-edge but inch perfect to secure what was also Alpine’s first pole. It represents a huge result for the team who are sixth in the world championship and have not been close to vying with the front four constructors this season.In a very tightly fought contest, the McLaren of Oscar Piastri was third fastest, but he was given a three-place grid penalty for impeding Liam Lawson. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were in fourth and fifth, with the latter saying he thought his title chance might be slipping away. Lando Norris – the defending world champion and winner of the past two races – was in ninth.Russell, who had been favourite to take the top spot was disappointed but took it well, admitting it was the second time that day Gasly had bested him. “We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying,” he said. “He beat me there and I thought: ‘Well, I think I’ll beat you in qualifying,’ and here we are, he’s ahead of me again.”Although he took seventh place, the championship leader, Kimi Antonelli, will start in 20th having taken a full set of new engine components, with Mercedes opting to do so at Monza because of the ample scope for overtaking at the circuit. They are hopeful he might come back to as high as fifth place, while Russell will be intent on making back a decent haul of points against his teammate. Antonelli leads Russell and Hamilton by 59 points.But the day belonged to Gasly and the Frenchman has shown form at Monza before, taking his only win here in 2020 in a race influenced by a well-timed pit stop and Hamilton, the pole-sitter, receiving a penalty. This pole was earned entirely on merit, but with the Mercedes likely to be formidable on race pace converting it will be a huge task, though doubtless not one from which the Frenchman will shirk.View image in fullscreenOn Thursday Pierre Gasly was stripped of his third-place finish in Monaco. Two days later he earned his first pole position.Photograph: Antonio Calanni/APBefore qualifying, the ICA issued a stern rebuttal to Briatore’s allegations. His comments alleged a judge, whom he named, had acted as a “prosecutor” and said: “The reason why so nasty, this guy. He is very linked with McLaren.” It prompted a fierce row, with the McLaren principal, Andrea Stella, dismissing the comments as “insulting” to his team.The ICA, which acts independently of the FIA, pointedly noted that Alpine had every chance to question the appointment of the judges but did not do so and that they were carefully selected.Formula One 2026: Pierre Gasly takes shock pole in Italian Grand Prix qualifying – as it happenedRead more“At both the beginning and conclusion of the hearing, the parties were invited to raise any issue concerning the proceedings or the composition of the court,” the statement said. “None did so. No objection was raised during the hearing concerning the manner in which the court questioned the witness or conducted the proceedings.“The FIA courts wish to make clear that the appointment and participation of the judges in that case, like for any other case, were conducted in accordance with the applicable FIA judicial procedures and usual practice, which are inspired by the highest standards like the International Bar Association guidelines on conflicts of interest in international arbitration.“They are all subject to the independence and confidentiality requirements contained in the FIA judicial and disciplinary rules, make annual disclosures of interests to the FIA compliance officer, and sign a specific declaration of independence for each particular case in consideration of the issue at stake and the parties involved, which is served to the parties.”Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Formula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Mali shock Spain for historic second win at Women’s Basketball World Cup | Fiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 | The Guardian
description: Sika Kone scores 19 points as Mali pull off tournament’s first major upset, while Hungary edge Nigeria for their first World Cup victory since 1998
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Sika Kone scores 19 points as Mali pull off tournament’s first major upset, while Hungary edge Nigeria for their first World Cup victory since 1998
Content: Mali’s Aminata Sangare celebrates after her team’s 82-73 victory over Spain in Berlin.Photograph: Armand Lenoir/FIBA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMali’s Aminata Sangare celebrates after her team’s 82-73 victory over Spain in Berlin.Photograph: Armand Lenoir/FIBA/Getty ImagesFiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026Mali shock Spain for historic second win at Women’s Basketball World CupKone has 19 points and 10 rebounds in 82-73 upsetHungary hold off Nigeria 71-67 for long-awaited winMali improve to 2-10 all-time at World CupAgenciesSat 5 Sep 2026 12.54 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMali pulled off the first stunner of the Women’sBasketballWorld Cup by shocking Spain 82-73 on Saturday.It was only the second win ever in tournament history for the African country, who beat Senegal in overtime in 2010.Caitlin Clark’s double-double helps USA rout China in Fiba World Cup openerRead moreMali was down two at the half, but outscored Spain 31-19 in the third quarter to take the lead. Mali went on a 16-4 run in that period after it was down 45-44 to take command. Sika Kone, who finished with 19 points, had two three-pointers during that game-changing run. Kone, who plays for the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA, also had 10 rebounds.Mali (1-1) scored the first five points of the fourth quarter, including another 3-pointer by Kone, to put the game away as Spain could get no closer than nine the rest of the way.Djeneba N’Diaye also had 19 points for Mali, which is 2-10 in their World Cup history.Iyana Martin scored 20 points for Spain (1-1), who were one of the top teams in the world.Hungary hold off Nigeria for first World Cup win in 28 yearsDorka Juhasz had 19 points and 16 rebounds to help Hungary edge Nigeria 71-67.Nigeria (0-2) were down 66-52 with 3:57 left before getting within two with 3 seconds left on Elizabeth Balogun’s basket. Nigeria fouled Reka Lelik with just over a second left and she calmly knocked down both free throws to seal the win.It was Hungary’s first victory since 1998 when the team topped China in the quarterfinals. Now they’ll play Korea next to close out pool play.Virag Takacs-Kiss added 17 points for Hungary (1-1). Juhasz, who plays for the Minnesota Lynx, had 13 points and 11 rebounds in the first half.Amy Okonkwo scored 17 points to lead Nigeria, which finishes off pool play against France.Other games on Saturday were Germany against Japan and France playing Korea.Explore more on these topicsFiba Women's Basketball World Cup 2026BasketballShareReuse this content

title: Haaland edges Manchester City past Coventry as Fernández sparkles on debut | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Erling Haaland scored the only goal of the game as Manchester City beat Coventry 1-0 at the Etihad
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Erling Haaland scored the only goal of the game as Manchester City beat Coventry 1-0 at the Etihad
Content: Erling Haaland beats Aurèle Amenda to the header to score the only goal of the game, and his 300th in club football.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersView image in fullscreenErling Haaland beats Aurèle Amenda to the header to score the only goal of the game, and his 300th in club football.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersPremier LeagueHaaland edges Manchester City past Coventry as Fernández sparkles on debutJamie Jacksonat the Etihad StadiumSat 5 Sep 2026 12.02 EDTLast modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 15.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnzo Fernández started forManchester Cityafter Nico O’Reilly’s back injury during the warm-up and sparkled, showing why the club paid a British-record-equalling £125m for the midfielder. The winner came courtesy of Erling Haaland’s 300th goal in club football and Fernández had a key part, feeding Antoine Semenyo, whose cross from the right was crashed home.In the second half Coventry hammered away, but their wait for a first top-flight goal since Mustapha Hadji’s second in a 3-2 defeat at Aston Villa on 5 May 2001 goes on. The visitors did not like losing, but were heartened by holding the star-studded hosts to a slender win, though the bottom line is all three of theirPremier Leagueoutings on their return have been defeats.Le Fée earns redemption and rescues point for Sunderland at BrentfordRead moreFrank Lampard said: “I don’t think we deserved to lose. I’m disappointed we didn’t get what we deserved – which was a point. We can walk out of here with our heads held extremely high.”Enzo Maresca’s men have a maximum nine points so can be supremely satisfied. “Today was not a nice win, a bit ugly,” he said. “In the first half we deserved more goals – we scored one but could have scored one or two more.”The manager said of Fernández: “The reason Enzo was on the bench [initially] was because he arrived only a few days ago. I know how frustrating it was for him in the last weeks but in the end he played some minutes and was quite good. Nico felt something in his back – not serious.”Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought for £85m, was on the bench for the hosts, as Fernández lined up alongside Rayan Cherki in a 4-1-2–2-1 that had Semenyo and Iliman Ndiaye, another new home signing, stationed behind Haaland.View image in fullscreenEnzo Fernández shoots on his Manchester City debut.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersCoventry, with Ethan Pinnock and Frank Onyeka replacing Caleb Yirenkyi and Loum Tchaouna from the XIthat lost at home to Hull, could have taken the lead when Abdukodir Khusanov played the ball back to Gianluigi Donnarumma and it slipped under the goalkeeper’s boot, but the Italian scrambled it clear. The visitors should then have bridged the 25 years to Hadji when a Semenyo pass meant for Rúben Dias was intercepted by Taiwo Awoniyi. But when the striker ran in his radar failed, and the shot was pulled wide.The longer Coventry stayed level the better their prospects. Cherki fed a galloping Haaland and he twisted and let fly, but Carl Rushworth’s save was equal to the shot. Then, dazzling Cherki footwork – after a pass from Fernández – was followed by an effort that struck a post.The frame of the goal and Rushworth could do nothing to stop Haaland’s opener. This time Fernández curved a pass in behind for Semenyo, the right-winger spun the ball over, and Haaland did the rest.This was 26 minutes in and Coventry were under siege. Fernández collected the ball along the right, looked up and aimed a cross for Haaland but it failed to beat the first man. Then Cherki, again in Fred Astaire mode, made space and saw an effort blocked.Maresca wants his wingers to be more direct – utilising the pace of Ndiaye and Semenyo – and the tactic spun Coventry. So, too, did an impish Cherki flick which put Haaland in again: he rode a challenge when going down might have brought a penalty, before shooting. Rushworth once more thwarted the Norwegian.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenFrank Lampard and the Coventry players applaud their fans but their wait for a Premier League goal goes on.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersFor Coventry, Jack Rudoni did better than Awoniyi with a header at close range, but Donnarumma flew to his left to prevent an equaliser. This showed the hope Lampard’s men carried but they had to finish any chance as these were scarce.Ndiaye was fairly quiet on debut and when Cherki’s work took the ball to him in the area he should have pulled the trigger but refused.Maresca said of the Senegalese: “Ili just had two sessions with us – most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, he needs to learn. When Marc Guéhi has the ball [at centre-back] he was dropping a lot – we didn’t need that, we needed him in the final third, that space was for Josko [Gvardiol, the left-back].”The manager was more enthused about Elliot Anderson. “Really impressed not just today, he was very good against Palace, and against Bournemouth,” said Maresca. “The best thing with Elliot is day by day he wants to be better.”Bouaddi’s home debut came on 75 minutes for Fernández and the 18-year-old showed composure during Coventry’s late-game bombardment, which included Ellis Sims forcing a point-blank save from Donnarumma.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueManchester CityCoventry Citymatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Uefa legal case may be beginning of the end for Infantino as Trump’s support evaporates | Fifa | The Guardian
description: The order of discovery related to Fifa’s failed plan to sell the World Cup will worry the American president, a situation that tends to end badly for the culprit
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: The order of discovery related to Fifa’s failed plan to sell the World Cup will worry the American president, a situation that tends to end badly for the culprit
Content: Gianni Infantino already looks to be running out of support in the light of being accused of ‘criminal mismanagement’ by Uefa.Illustration: Cameron Law/The GuardianView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino already looks to be running out of support in the light of being accused of ‘criminal mismanagement’ by Uefa.Illustration: Cameron Law/The GuardianFifaUefa legal case may be beginning of the end for Infantino as Trump’s support evaporatesBarney RonayThe order of discovery related to Fifa’s failed plan to sell the World Cup will worry the American president, a situation that tends to end badly for the culpritSat 5 Sep 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 06.34 EDTShare“Tell Mike it was just business. I always liked him.”“He understands.”“Tom, can you get me off the hook? For old times’ sake?”“Sorry can’t do it.”I never believed it would actually happen. Not really. Not until this week, when, for the first time, there was a sense, as The Godfather makes so abundantly clear, that you really can get to anyone.Fifa calls Uefa’s legal threat a ‘smear campaign’ in US federal filingRead moreGianni Infantino is beleaguered.Gianni Infantinois re-beleaguered. Gianni Infantino has been beleaguered for almost six weeks, since news emerged of his grotesque undercover plan to sell off, for related personal gain, the shared global property he’s employed to preserve, protect and safely pass on.There has been hopeful talk in that time of toxic status attained, a base being hollowed out,a rival presidential candidatenext March. But power runs deep. Entrenched dictatorial power runs even deeper. Time passes. The doorway narrows. Infantino is already the man who sold the world, not once, but twice, most recently to Donald Trumpin return for a peace prize, a scrunchie and a fawning presence around the sub-table of power.Give it a month. Chuck in a Football Jesus turn at the lighted lectern a few weeks from now, arms whirling like a street magician, reeling off the usual stuff about caring and sharing, égalité, fraternité, fiscal stimuli. Look deep into those weirdly flat painted-on eyes, cold and hard behind the papier-mache mask of power. You don’t buy me out. I buy you out.But something has shifted this week. It was never going to be the gnats around his ankles that did for Infantino: another thundering newspaper column, the latest stern denouncement from – whoah, hang on – former Manchester United utility defender Mikaël Silvestre.Hard power is something else, however. And two things have now happened, both responses to thethreat of a Uefa lawsuit, which I believe has no really serious notions of ultimate victory, but which may turn out to be an expert chess move, a zugzwang that leaves the king having to go somewhere, but with no safe spaces left to hide.View image in fullscreenJosh Kushner said he ‘would not have gotten involved’ in Fifa’s plans had he known the full picture.Photograph: Brendan McDermid/ReutersThe first response was Josh Kushner’s statement this week after being named as a party to discovery in Florida. Kushner was the money guy behind theFifaForward fiasco. Nuts isn’t it? The person you come to for finance and macro-favour just happens to be, by an accident of talent and destiny, the brother of the president’s son-in-law.Kushner said he “would not have gotten involved” in Fifa’s plans had he known the full picture. He said this was all regrettable. Ostensibly mild and reasonable words, but with a sense of distance being carved out, of a cutting loose from the protective apron.Kushner has also hired a nuclear option lawyer, Alex Spiro, who defended Elon Musk when he called a caver “a pedo” and Alec Baldwin when he accidentally shot someone. It’s a serious defensive move. As is, to a more rattled degree,Fifa’s counter-filing this week, which dismisses the whole episode as a “smear campaign”, then says the quiet thing out loud. Specifically, Fifa mentions discovery and a very urgent intention to resist it.This is the real point. No one on the Infantino side wants discovery. Which is, to be clear, the sharing of related documents, from internal memos down to relevant emails sent from your smartphone on the golf course after lunch.This, as Gianni knows, is always a worry to those in power. And you really don’t want to be a worry to anyone in any way connected to Trump. This is why, behind the sabre rattling, there is for the first time a sense of a thinning out, of nobody there on the ward, no cops on the doors, of the old man up there unprotected.Even Trump’s early support for Infantino was a little over-juiced in the media. The president Truth Socialed his assurances in early August. It still felt a little qualified. “If for any reason” Fifa got rid of Infantino, well, this would be really bad. And nothing since.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThere is a vague sense of a shrug here, of an amble away from the stage. We remember the good times for the Gianni-Trump bro-tocracy, laughing together like men in a Brooks Brothers senior knitwear advert, the gleaming bald impresario to power and his tolerant daddy-patron looking as ever like a giant man-size unit of American food, as though something deep-fried, honey-glazed and dished up at an out-of-town hotel conference buffet has somehow learned to walk around in a baggy suit and say things like “a very tall, very handsome man”.View image in fullscreen‘Zip it’: Fifa will want to avoid discovery to protect Gianni Infantino’s relationship with Donald Trump.Photograph: Shawn Thew/EPAThis is always brittle. Trump will walk you in, remember your name, glad-hand you by the stairwell. But once you’re gone you really are gone. There is no loyalty, and logically so, because Trumpian politics has no core belief, no substance, just a cold, hard matrix of winners and losers.And if you lose, or look like you might, then by coincidence bad things tend to happen. The Guardian published a list a while back of Trump enemies whonow find themselves subject to charges, exile, security clearances revoked, mortgage fraud investigated. And that list does include some pretty high-profile one-time golden boys.Michael Cohen, the fiercest of Trump loyalists, who famously stated he would “take a bullet” for the big man? Legal difficulties and fallings-out intervened. Cohen has since been imprisoned, disbarred and sent into exile. The former US attorney general Jeff Sessions was among the first to call Trumpism “a movement”. He’s now not only out of the game, but has apparently been described by Trump, variously, as weak, confused, dumb, an idiot, a disgrace, and “mentally retarded”. There is a pattern here. If you’re in then you’re in. But don’t fly too close to those flames.The decision of the court on allowing discovery could well be key. Make no mistake, Uefa is accusing Fifa and Infantino of “criminal mismanagement”. The key issue is an alleged undervaluing in the sale of the World Cup. Unrelated, and arguably standard industry practice, Infantino also stood to take a huge personal salary from all this.It is a clear attempt to peer inside and see what, if anything, is in that box. Uefa wants discovery from Fifa, Thrive Capital and the Trump donor and deal adviser Greg Maffei, all of whom will have paper trails from that period when Infantino was granted intoxicating access to the halls of power. It puts you in mind of the Club World Cup trophy, a weird, frightening-looking thing, all razor-sharp odd nooks and crannies, the secret little drawer full of human toenails. Do you really want to know what’s in there? Is it safe to look?“Please Mike, don’t do this, don’t do this to me”“Today I settle all the family business. So don’t tell me you’re innocent.”How is this going to play out? Infantino is doing what he can, touring his outer provinces and pressing the flesh. Saudi Arabia has offered qualified backing (“at this time …”). There’s a Fifa congress in November. Really, though, you wonder about votes, and to what extent votes are the thing here. It is hard not to muse on how it ended in football for Sepp Blatter and Michel Platini. That one-shot illegal payment allegation really did come out of the blue.For now the process will simmer on. Legal challenges often fail or melt away. Uefa just needs to keep pressing, to make it clear that coals will be raked. Keep the pressure up and you never know what may fall out, or from where. Mr president, you can have my answer now. Our offer is this. Nothing.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoFootball politicscommentShareReuse this content

title: Vuelta a España: Marco Brenner wins stage 14 but extreme heat forces shorter stage 15 | Vuelta a España | The Guardian
description: Marco Brenner kicked to the finish to take his first Grand Tour stage – and the first for the Tudor team – while Enric Mas retained the red jersey
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Marco Brenner kicked to the finish to take his first Grand Tour stage – and the first for the Tudor team – while Enric Mas retained the red jersey
Content: Marco Brenner made a telling kick at the last to deny Santiago Buitrago victory.Photograph: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMarco Brenner made a telling kick at the last to deny Santiago Buitrago victory.Photograph: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty ImagesVuelta a EspañaVuelta a España: Marco Brenner wins stage 14 but extreme heat forces shorter stage 15Mas retains red jersey; stage 15 to be shortenedTadej Pogacar to miss rest of season after surgeryGuardian sportand agenciesSat 5 Sep 2026 13.21 EDTFirst published on Sat 5 Sep 2026 07.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGermany’s Marco Brenner fought off the Bahrain Victorious rider Santiago Buitrago to claim victory in stage 14 of theVuelta a España– a first Grand Tour stage win both for the rider and his Tudor team. However, organisers later announced that 40C-plus temperatures on Sunday had caused them to shorten Sunday’s 189.7km stage from Palma del Río to Córdoba to a 110.2km stage.In a climactic duel, Brenner tailed Buitrago ⁠into the last 500m and timed his kick superbly, gritting his teeth as he sped ahead during the ascent to Sierra de La Pandera, finishing one second ahead of the Colombian.The overall leader Enric Mas (Movistar), finishing 22nd in the stage, gained around 25 seconds on the veteran four-time Vuelta winner Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), who slipped from second to third in the general classification behind Felix Gall of the Decathlon CMA CGM team. Gall trails Mas by 2min 6sec in the race for the red jersey.View image in fullscreenEnric Mas suffered a technical blip during stage 14 but emerged unscathed and actually stretched his overall lead to 2min 6sec.Photograph: Javier Lizón/EPACarlos Rodríguez (Netcompany Ineos) finished the stage third at the end of the 154.5km ride from Jaén to La Pandera. He moved up to eighth overall having started the day 17th in the general classification.“I cannot really believe it yet,” said the 24-year-old Brenner of his stage win. “I was struggling with some sickness earlier in the race and had a crash, but I really wanted to show myself and also my teammates that I can be ‌up there.”The peloton was nearly seven minutes behind when Kevin Vermaerke made a solo attack on the descent from Los Villares, with about 40km left in the stage.Mas ignored ​an early breakaway of more than 40 riders, and stayed calm as he suffered a mechanical issue that made him briefly stop. Roglic and Gall stayed close to the red jersey holder, who remained in the peloton until the final climb.With 20km left, Rodríguez joined a group of attackers to chase down Vermaerke. They caught the solo leader during the 12km ⁠climb to Sierra de La Pandera but in the final 5km Buitrago and Brenner ​sped ahead of the rest.“I made ​the move, Santiago passed me but I ​could catch up, and in the end I could beat him in the sprint ... you live ​for days like today, ‌I guess,” said Brenner.Mas ​attacked in the final kilometres ​and Gall managed to stay on his wheel but Roglic, who trailed Mas by 1:45 coming into the stage, could not keep up, allowing the Spaniard to achieve an increased cushion.Of the stage 15 alteration, Vuelta organisers said: “With the aim of protecting the health of the riders and ensuring the best possible conditions for the competition, the Extreme Weather Protocol is being activated. The stage will cover 110.2km, instead of the 189.7km originally planned. The route modification will take effect from kilometre 52.”Tadej Pogacar will end his season prematurely after undergoing surgery on the fractured collarbone sustained in acrash at the Vuelta, he said on Saturday, with the injury ruling him out of this month’s world championships.View image in fullscreenTadej Pogacar – pictured in the Tour de France in July – sustained a concussion and cervical fracture, along with multiple cuts and bruises, in his crash at the Vuelta.Photograph: Garnier Etienne/Reuters“Of course, this isn’t the way I wanted my season to finish. Right now, the most important thing is to recover properly and give my body the time it needs,” Pogacar said in a UAE Team Emirates statement.At the same time the team also announced Pogacar had signed a contract extension through to the end of the 2032 season. “From the beginning, this team has felt like home for me. We have grown together over the years and shared some incredible moments, so I’m very happy to extend my contract until 2032,” said Pogacar. “There is still a lot I want to achieve in this sport and I believe this is the right place to do it.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“It has been a season with many special moments and I’m proud of what we achieved together. Now I’ll focus on getting healthy, supporting the guys from home, and coming back next year ready for what’s ahead.”Tour of Britain: Bol wins stage; Wellens in chargeCees Bol claimed his firstTour of Britainstage win since 2022 with victory at stage four, but Tim Wellens’s mid-race attack ensured he took over as general classification leader.View image in fullscreenTim Wellens (right) ahead of Cees Bol on stage four of the Tour of Britain.Photograph: Zac Williams/SWpix.com/ShutterstockThe 165.8km stage between Helmsley and Leyburn was initially led by a six-man break which included Decathlon CMA CGM Team rider Bol.However, Wellens of UAE Team Emirates-XRG produced an attack with around 42km left and it paid dividends.Wellens and Bol then worked together to establish a healthy lead until the stage-ending sprint.Bol successfully pulled out the finish needed for the win while Wellens crossed three seconds later, overtaking overnight leader Lewis Askey.Press AssociationExplore more on these topicsVuelta a EspañaTour of BritainCyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Jacob Ramsey comes in from the cold as Newcastle peg back Bournemouth | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Jacob Ramsey came off the bench to earn Newcastle a 2-2 draw as Bournemouth dropped points in the dying minutes for a third straight match
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: Jacob Ramsey came off the bench to earn Newcastle a 2-2 draw as Bournemouth dropped points in the dying minutes for a third straight match
Content: Bournemouth were left wondering what might have been again when Jacob Ramsey equalised for Newcastle in the 88th minute.Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PAView image in fullscreenBournemouth were left wondering what might have been again when Jacob Ramsey equalised for Newcastle in the 88th minute.Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PAPremier LeagueJacob Ramsey comes in from the cold as Newcastle peg back BournemouthLouise Taylorat St James' ParkSat 5 Sep 2026 09.44 EDTLast modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 16.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJust as Bournemouth’s Alex Scott seemed to have succeeded in building a personal playground by the Tyne, another midfielder emerged from the shadows and stripped the shine from his afternoon.Since Matthias Jaissle succeeded Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s manager Jacob Ramsey has been largely shunted to the margins but the home substitute’s superbly executed 88th-minute equaliser ensured Scott and his teammates needed to settle for a point.Newcastle United 2-2 Bournemouth: Premier League – as it happenedRead moreFor a third straightPremier Leaguegame Bournemouth’s new manager, Marco Rose, watched his side surrender a lead as much stellar passing and movement on Scott’s part was ultimately eclipsed.“Newcastle had two shots on target and we conceded twice,” said Rose, whose side were 2-0 up at one point and had 17 shots on target. “Newcastle had no real solutions to our first-half pressing and, then, more or less from nothing, we conceded.”Like Jaissle, Rose is a German graduate of the Red Bull coaching school and former RB Salzburg manager. Big on verticality, intensity and relentless pressing, both men have much in common but systems are only as good as the players within them and, in Scott, Rose possessed a player blessed with the brain and vision to dominate central midfield. “I love Alex,” said Rose. “I’m so proud and happy he’s a Bournemouth player.”View image in fullscreenMarcus Tavernier’s second league goal of the season put Bournemouth ahead.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersNewcastle’s manager knew he had been slightly fortunate in denying his compatriot a first win of the season. “It’s something special to come back after being 2-0 down,” said Jaissle. “But there’s mixed feelings. The two goals we conceded were a bit slapstick. We’re still on a learning curve.”It became a little steeper in the ninth minute when Scott’s shot was deflected into Marcus Tavernier’s path and the latter’s rapid reaction resulted in his deft finish whizzing past Lukas Hornicek.As Newcastle’s rearguard continued to wobble, with Sven Botman looking particularly vulnerable, Evanilson spurned a chance to make Rose jump for joy for a second time. Jaissle was receiving a reminder as to why the name Bournemouth is synonymous with banana skin on Tyneside.Newcastle, after all, have now failed to beat their guests from Dorset in any of the pair’s last nine Premier League meetings.Once again the visitors seemed to be finding the north-east air hugely restorative. Indeed, as the minutes ticked by, it appeared as if a malicious cyberhacker had somehow programmed Newcastle’s players to forfeit possession at every opportunity. Jaissle’s team appeared at once cowed and overwhelmed by Rose’s ruthlessly clever press.At this stage the only puzzle was how Bournemouth, with Scott increasingly impressive, were not at least 3-0 ahead. After failing to polish off a series of chances, Bournemouth eventually made it 2-0 when Justin Kluivert unleashed a high velocity shot from distance that rebounded off a combination of a post and Hornicek before dropping to Scott.All that remained was for Malick Thiaw to register an own goal after deflecting Scott’s cross-shot beyond Hornicek.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenAlex Scott (left) played an important role in the goals that put Bournemouth 2-0 up after 35 minutes.Photograph: Scott Heppell/ReutersRose raced down the touchline in celebration only to, metaphorically, fall flat on his face two minutes later when the previously frustrating Harvey Barnes cut inside from the left and curled a wonderful shot past Dorde Petrovic after collecting Lewis Hall’s intelligent pass.Perhaps galvanised by Jaissle’s half-time homily Newcastle improved. They came tantalisingly close to equalising when Joe Willock’s glancing header flashed fractionally off target following Yoane Wissa’s excellent cross and Elanga’s flick-on. Suddenly, Rose looked distinctly nervous.The moment had arrived for Jaissle to introduce his new £51m attacking signing. This time last week Matias Fernandez-Pardo was a Lille forward but now he was making his Newcastle debut in the No 10 role behind Wissa.Bournemouth though refused to fold and Jaissle received a yellow card for persistently stepping outside his technical area while repeatedly offering the fourth official a piece of his mind.View image in fullscreenHarvey Barnes scored a terrific goal to halve Newcastle’s deficit.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersNo matter; his mood brightened appreciably in the 88th minute. When Bournemouth failed to clear the fallout from Jacob Murphy’s cross, the ball fell, eventually, to another home substitute returning from the periphery.Ramsey needed no second invitation to make his presence felt, striking the ball low and cleanly into the bottom corner. “It’s been a bit disappointing not to play more,” he said. “But, hopefully, I’ve shown I’m more than capable.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueNewcastle UnitedBournemouthmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Arteta v Alonso, part one: a desire for control and the theory behind the chaos | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso prepare for an intriguing tactical battle in the first Premier League meeting between these two old friends
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso prepare for an intriguing tactical battle in the first Premier League meeting between these two old friends
Content: Mikel Arteta (left) and Xabi Alonso grew up in the same youth ranks, but have different managerial philosophies.Composite: PA, ReutersView image in fullscreenMikel Arteta (left) and Xabi Alonso grew up in the same youth ranks, but have different managerial philosophies.Composite: PA, ReutersChelseaArteta v Alonso, part one: a desire for control and the theory behind the chaosJonathan WilsonMikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso prepare for an intriguing tactical battle in the first Premier League meeting between old friendsSat 5 Sep 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 15.02 EDTShareControl v chaos. On the one hand, the forces of order, regimented, playing in precise patterns and, on the other, something darker, more visceral, a method that acknowledges the imperfection of the human soul, the unknowability of football in all its randomness; better, that second way says, to attempt to ride the fury than to believe it might be harnessed.When it began, a decade ago, that’s how the Pep Guardiola v Jürgen Klopp rivalry appeared. Apollo v Dionysius. Two fundamentally opposed ways of seeing the world. But in time, the two crept towards each other. Klopp moved away from the heavy metal of his Borussia Dortmund years to something more conservative. Guardiola experimented in multiple directions, slowly abandoning the possession-oriented idealism of his past to something less radical but also less predictable.‘Reverse bucket list’: Arteta channels Wenger in defence of Arsenal windowRead moreThe temptation, after the first two weeks of the season, is to cast Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso in a similar light. Arsenal are yet to concede a goal. They dominated the Community Shield from the first minute,beat a shambolic Manchester City 3-0and gave the sense that they could easily have won more comprehensively had they been minded to do so. They were no more troubled inbeating Coventry by the same scorelinein their opening league game and, while they were rather less dominant,they were still extremely comfortable against Aston Villa on Mondayand had been slowly increasing the pressure when Bukayo Saka gave them the lead just before the hour.Arteta has become more controlling over his seven years atArsenal, not just in his micromanagement but in his demands from his team. Tactical plans are sophisticated and negotiable only in the final details. In their third successive season of finishing second he spoke repeatedly of the need to reduce, to zero if possible, the xG of the opposition. If they have no chances, they cannot score, and if they do not score, they cannot win.Last season it was a refrain heard less often; Arsenal did reduce their opponents’ opportunities, conceding seven goals fewer than they had the previous season. There were those who criticised them on aesthetic grounds, bemoaning their reliance on set plays and occasional bouts of excessive pragmatism, but it worked. They were the best team and they won the league, in the end, fairly comfortably. All else is taste, subjective.Might, it will be asked, there be a more expansive approach this season? Might, with the burdens of yearning and doubt lifted, the insistence on control lessen? Might this be a breezier, a freer and easier, Arsenal? Might that even make them more effective in Europe, more capable ofbeating Paris Saint-Germain?View image in fullscreenBukayo Saka scores Arsenal’s winner at Aston Villa on Monday.Photograph: David Klein/ReutersProbably not. Arsenal played as they did in the Champions League final out of necessity, not choice. They were exhausted. Only three PSG players had played more than 2,000 minutes in the league last season; nine Arsenal players had – and given the relative strengths of the Premier League and Ligue 1, theirs were harder minutes. In such circumstances an open game is impossible.Accepting the role played by fatigue, in fact, has been one of Arsenal’s great strengths; last summer’s business was characterised by the accumulation of squad depth over acquisition of the very highest quality. This summer has been about upgrading where possible. They’ve seemingly done that well in midfield and at the back, although losing three players who can operate from the left wing while signing only Christos Tzolis seems a risk, even with Max Dowman likely to be more involved. It’s possible, likely even, that a more relaxed outlook will allow Arsenal to play with a greater freedom but it would be a surprise if the tactical emphasis were not still on control.Chelsea’s case is more complex; the sense of chaos of Alonso’s opening two games has surely not been deliberate. He is no Kloppite; his heritage is of John Toshack and Rafa Benítez, Vicente Del Bosque and Guardiola. Like Arteta, four months his junior, he came through the youth ranks at Antiguoko in San Sebastián; they are not so different in their formation. When Alonso won the league at Bayer Leverkusen, they had 62% possession. Although they pressed hard, they were not part of the high-tempo, high-turnover Bundesliga trend. Yet inbeating Fulham 3-2, Chelsea had 38% possession, and inbeating Brighton 4-3they had only 26%.Game state is partly responsible. In both games,Chelseahad the lead early and could afford to allow their opponents the ball. The front three of João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers have excelled playing on the break. There have been glimmers of the sort of interactions Leverkusen produced, the modifications that prevent Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 from experiencing the blockishness that means the formation is more often a tool for counterattacking sides, most notably when Maxence Lacroix advanced from central defence to set up Rogers’ goal against Fulham. But they take time to develop; perhaps the idea for now, as patterns are assimilated, is to lean into the basic simplicity of shape, the security the two screening midfielders in front of the back three should offer.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenChelsea have won their opening two Premier League games this season.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Nigel French/Apl/SportsphotoThe problem is, it hasn’t yet worked – although that may in part be down to personnel. Having sold Enzo Fernández without signing another central midfielder, though, Chelsea look short in midfield (in as much their bloated squad can look short of anything). If Roméo Lavia can remain fit, and if Reece James’s minutes can continue to be rationed, the issue should not be insoluble, but Moisés Caicedo’s knee problem complicates things, especially with Alonso seemingly unwilling yet to trust the 22-year-old Argentinian Valentín Barco from the start. Without Caicedo, that is not a midfield that is going to create much, and may struggle even with ball retention.Chelsea hit bullseye with Morgan Rogers as Arsenal rue what might have beenRead moreIt’s possible that on Sunday, in a game Chelsea are not expected to win, it is easier to maintain shape and discipline, that a destructive pairing works more naturally. Only by making the game a midfield slog to be decided by which team’s forward line can best exploit breakdowns can Chelsea feel they have an edge. That may end up looking like control against chaos, like possession against turnovers. It may even be so. But for Alonso that is a matter less of ideology than of expediency.Explore more on these topicsChelseaXabi AlonsoArsenalMikel ArtetacommentShareReuse this content

title: Glasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against Spurs | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Neco Williams had a goal disallowed for handball as Nottingham Forest drew 0-0 with Tottenham, and Oliver Glasner argued the evidence was unclear
Author: Ben Fisher
Headline: Neco Williams had a goal disallowed for handball as Nottingham Forest drew 0-0 with Tottenham, and Oliver Glasner argued the evidence was unclear
Content: Neco Williams had a goal disallowed for handball in the second half.Photograph: Chris Radburn/ReutersView image in fullscreenNeco Williams had a goal disallowed for handball in the second half.Photograph: Chris Radburn/ReutersPremier LeagueGlasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against SpursBen Fisherat the City GroundSat 5 Sep 2026 13.59 EDTFirst published on Sat 5 Sep 2026 12.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOliver Glasner argued there was insufficient evidence to disallow Neco Williams’s goal against Tottenham, accusing the video assistant referee Peter Bankes of guessing that theNottingham Forestdefender handled and said ruling it out weakens the officials’ authority. Midway through the second half, Williams stooped to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali attempted to hook the ball clear after Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbled towards the net.Glasner conceded at least one angle showed Williams appeared to handle the ball, seemingly to protect himself as Tonali went to clear the ball with his left boot, but said the footage was too unclear to disallow the goal. “I don’t think VAR can intervene when he’s guessing,” said Forest’s head coach. “It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention should be very high and this is why it was a wrong intervention for me.Chilwell seals Crystal Palace comeback win after Mitchell double at FulhamRead more“I’ve watched five or six different angles and to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt [of Williams] moves a little bit, but it’s not clear whether it’s [because of] the ball or Tonali on the goalline. I know refereeing aPremier Leaguegame is really difficult – refereeing a training session is sometimes really difficult – but we are told to support the referee, to keep the threshold for VAR intervention very high, to strengthen the referee’s decision and they didn’t do that today. With these kinds of situations, you weaken the referees.”Bankes checked the goal and then the referee, Craig Pawson, took to the mic before awarding a Spurs free-kick amid a chorus of boos from the home support: “After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest’s No 3 before the goal is scored.” Williams was adamant he did not handle the ball. “I headed it in between my arms,” said the Wales defender, who this week signed a new four-year contract. “If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t. I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms because it never. I knew straight away I’d headed it down in between my arms.”The disallowed goal was undeniably the moment of an underwhelming contest. For the third successive league match, Tottenham failed to score and this time they did not even muster a shot on target. Dominic Solanke heading on to the roof of the Forest goal, 88 minutes on the clock, was as threatening as they got. Omar Marmoush wellied a shot wide after Spurs countered at speed. Mykhailo Mudryk was brought off the bench for his first competitive minutes for 645 days after a doping suspension but Spurs were blunt. Aside from a5-1 win against a Charlton B teamin the Carabao Cup, their season so far reads: five goals against and none scored.View image in fullscreenSpurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk came on as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersApart from Gibbs-White’s effort in the buildup to the disallowed goal, Forest’s only other shot on goal was a daisy-cutter from James McAtee. TheSpurs league debutant Sávio, a £75m arrival from Manchester City, showed a few neat touches but he and Destiny Udogie were withdrawn after an hour on the advice of Tottenham’s medical department. “I’m not happy when we have the plan but it is for my advantage, my business, the management of the players after their injuries,” said De Zerbi, who accepted his team lacked quality in the final third. “We have to make better decisions, to keep more calm when we are very close to do something important.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNo wonder both teams remain winless. Spurs’s date at home to Everton next weekend has taken on another layer of significance and the same applies to Forest’s trip to Aston Villa. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive in attendance, could be forgiven for wondering when Spurs will see the fruits of their £300m-plus spend, much of the focus on sharpening their attack. They turned to Mudryk, who thrived under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, after the failure to sell Richarlison halted moves for preferred targets Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. This was not the desired result. “We bought very, very good players but you can’t just build the team with the names like in Football Manager,” De Zerbi said.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueNottingham ForestTottenham HotspurVideo assistant referees (VARs)match reportsShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St Mirren | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Celtic came from behind to win 2-1 at St Mirren, while Rangers lost Lawrence Shankland to injury but Ryan Naderi scored in a 1-0 victory against Motherwell
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Celtic came from behind to win 2-1 at St Mirren, while Rangers lost Lawrence Shankland to injury but Ryan Naderi scored in a 1-0 victory against Motherwell
Content: Yang Hyun-jun slots home to put Celtic 2-1 ahead of St Mirren.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAView image in fullscreenYang Hyun-jun slots home to put Celtic 2-1 ahead of St Mirren.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St MirrenCeltic come from behind to win 2-1 at St MirrenRangers beat Motherwell 1-0 but lose Shankland to injuryPress AssociationSat 5 Sep 2026 17.36 EDTFirst published on Sat 5 Sep 2026 12.34 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleYang Hyun-jun scored the winner asCelticcame from behind to beat an impressiveSt Mirrenside 2-1.St Mirrenwere heading for the top of the Premiership when Nikolas Agrafiotis netted from the spot midway through the first half.Liam Scales conceded the penalty with a handball but made amends when he headed home six minutes after the break. And Yang finished off a counterattack midway through the second half after good pressing from Camilo Durán.The victory in Paisley made it five wins from five league games for the champions and inflicted St Mirren’s first Premiership defeat. Martin O’Neill’s side were made to work all the way by a Saints side who played with tempo, invention and managed 19 shots at goal.O’Neill later lamented the unavailability of Yang for some crucial games – the 24-year-old will now fly to Japan for the Asian Games and miss the midweek trip to St Johnstone and two games againstRangers, plus the Europa League opener against Ferencvaros.“We are going to miss him. He’s in really fine form at the moment,” the manager said. “But he’s signed off with a brilliant goal. He’s in great form and he’ll work for you going backwards. He doesn’t mind doing the hard graft.”Rangersstriker Ryan Naderi accepted a gift to score the only goal againstMotherwellat Ibrox, but they fear their captain Lawrence Shankland faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines after a hamstring injury suffered early on in the game.Naderi, who came on for Shankland in the eighth minute, dispossessed Alex Paulsen as the Motherwell goalkeeper attempted to dribble the ball past him outside his box and the German had the simple task of rolling the ball into the net to score what proved to be a 12th-minute winner.Motherwell dominated possession and created several chances but Rangers were more effective in the final third and should have added to their lead. Kim Min-su missed a first-half penalty and the debutant striker Kevin Kelsy was among those to pass up good opportunities after he came off the bench.View image in fullscreenLawrence Shankland leaves the pitch unaided but his manager later revealed the club fear his hamstring injury is significant.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PARangers ultimately saw out the game without any late scares as they recorded a third consecutive Premiership victory.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOf Shankland, the Rangers manager, Derek McInnes, said he fears the injury is similarly significant to the one that kept him out for two months early in 2026. McInnes said: “He has a similar feeling to the hamstring injury he had at Hearts last January. We don’t want to speculate too much but he says it feels similar, in the same area, so we’ll get him scanned on Monday.“He says he felt fine going into the game and there was nothing really that he did in the game that he was aware of, he just felt it pull up. It’s a shame for the boy because he was obviously in good form, getting himself moving and enjoying some of that attacking threat we’ve had over the last few games, and we’ve waited long and hard for that.”Michael Forbes scored an added-time equaliser forDundee UnitedagainstFalkirk, who had led at Tannadice thanks to Jacob Murrell’s fourth-minute opener, whileKilmarnockpicked up their first point but are still waiting for a first Premiership win of the season after a 0-0 draw atAberdeen. Kilmarnock’s Aaron Tshibola was sent off for a second yellow card after 83 minutes but the hosts could not find a way past the 10 men.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipCelticRangersMotherwellSt MirrenAberdeenKilmarnocknewsShareReuse this content

title: European football: Martínez seals thrilling comeback for unbeaten Inter | European club football | The Guardian
description: Serie A champions Inter secured a late comeback victory over Napoli, while Roma went top of the table with two ultra-late goals against Atalanta
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Serie A champions Inter secured a late comeback victory over Napoli, while Roma went top of the table with two ultra-late goals against Atalanta
Content: Lautaro Martínez scored twice for Serie A leaders Inter on Saturday.Photograph: Matteo Bazzi/EPAView image in fullscreenLautaro Martínez scored twice for Serie A leaders Inter on Saturday.Photograph: Matteo Bazzi/EPAEuropean club footballEuropean football: Martínez seals thrilling comeback for unbeaten InterChampions Inter and Roma pull off stunning comebacksSchalke 0-0 Bayern Munich; Hoffenheim 2-3 DortmundGuardian sportand agenciesSat 5 Sep 2026 15.50 EDTFirst published on Sat 5 Sep 2026 12.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLautaro Martínez scored in the 91st minute asInterrallied from two goals down ⁠to secure a stunning 3-2 home victory overNapoli, continuing their 100% start to their ⁠Serie A title defence.Napoli looked ⁠to be ​on course for victory when Matteo Politano and Rasmus Højlund put them 2-0 up after 53 minutes, but Martínez’s ⁠first goal halved the deficit and Marcus Thuram equalised eight minutes from the end. Both sides had excellent chances to win ⁠it after that but it was Inter who took theirs when the Argentinian stabbed ​home the ball at the back ‌post from a corner.After ‌no goals in the first half, the game burst into life on 50 ‌minutes when Politano finished from a rebound. Three minutes after that Højlund collected Giovanni di Lorenzo’s pass and scored with a shot that arrowed in from the edge of the box.José Mourinho sick as a Parrott as Real Madrid sunk by Real Betis and Irish supersubRead moreInter hit back three minutes later though as Martínez provided a clinical finish, and Thuram’s header from Carlos Augusto’s pass ‌levelled the scores.It was anybody’s game from there as the action went back and forth between the two boxes, but Inter ​found the momentum they needed to take the points.Romascored twice past the 90th minute to claim a 2-1 ​victory overAtalantaand move to the top following a dramatic clash at the Stadio Olimpico.Éderson’s opener for Atalanta looked to be steering them to victory, but Roma equalised through Mario Hermoso’s looping header.They were not content with the point though and continued to push forward, allowing Matías Soulé to score via a loose ball in the box in ⁠the 93rd minute to snatch all three points.Torinoclaimed a first win under Ignazio Abate when they came from behind to win 2-1 atFiorentina.Fiorentina took the lead when Mateo Pellegrino tried a shot from range that should have been a comfortable ⁠stop for Lucas Perri, but theTorinogoalkeeper allowed the ball ​to squirm beyond ​him.Perri later made several good ​saves to keep his side in the contest, before the ​visitors turned the ‌game on its ​head. Rolando Mandragora drilled ​the ball into the Fiorentina net from outside the box to level the score at 1-1, before Ché Adams poked home from close range on 82 minutes to secure all three points for the away side.Later on Saturday, Gian Piero Gasperini faces his former clubAtalantawhen they visitRoma.View image in fullscreenHarry Kane and Bayern Munich were held to a rare goalless draw in the Bundesliga at Schalke.Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/ReutersIn the Bundesliga,Bayern Munichwere left to rue several missed chances in the second half by Harry Kane and Luiz Díaz in their stalemate at Schalke. Loris Karius made several outstanding saves as the visitors failed to score in a Bundesliga game for the first time since a draw atBayer Leverkusenin February 2025.Kane and Michael Olise started on the bench, Bayern dominated the ball but created few clear chances, and stubbornSchalkedug deep to pick up their first point of the season.Jamal Musiala played his first league minutes of the season after the Bayern midfielder collapsed in two pre-season games due to a neurological issue which causes seizures.The Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri caused a late own goal inBorussia Dortmund’s favour, as his side came from two down to win 3-2 atHoffenheimin a topsy-turvy clash.Hoffenheim were the better team for the opening hour but lost their way as Dortmund clicked into gear and romped to victory with three goals in the final 30 minutes.Hoffenheim were two up with 54 minutes played thanks to goals from Leon Avdullahu and Tim Lemperle. Nwaneri, who became the youngest player in Premier League history in 2024, arrived on a season-long loan from Arsenal on deadline day and came on with half an hour played after an injury for Filippo Mane.Serhou Guirassy gave the hosts hope when he scored just after the hour mark and then set up Fábio Silva five minutes later.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWith just four minutes of regular time remaining, Nwaneri cut down the left and shot centrally, but his effort took a big deflection off the home defender Albian Hajdari and into the goal.The Bundesliga newcomersElversbergcontinued their excellent top-flight arrival with a 4-3 win atBorussia Mönchengladbach, making it two wins from two this season.Gladbach took the lead twice and were 3-1 up midway through the second-half, but Elversberg fought back despite losing manager Vincent Wagner to a second yellow card just before the break.With 10 minutes left, Felix Keidel levelled the scores at 3-3 and Maurice Krattenmacher put the visitors in front in stoppage time with his second goal of the match.Bayer Leverkusenrebounded from their loss to Elversberg last Saturday by putting sorryUnion Berlinto the sword in a 4-0 home victory.Argentina internationals Equi Fernández and Facundo Medina had Leverkusen 2-0 up at half-time. The England centre-back Jarell Quansah set up Patrik Schick for Leverkusen’s third before Ibrahim Maza added a stylish fourth late on.West Ham loanee Niclas Füllkrug scored his second goal in three games since returning to Germany to helpWerder Bremenwin at home 3-1 againstRB Leipzig. The Germany striker scored a long-range header, with Eren Dinkci and Marco Grüll also getting on the scoresheet.Last season’s Europa League finalistsFreiburgcontinued their perfect start to the season with a solid 1-0 win at promotedPaderborn.View image in fullscreenOihan Sancet roars with delight after scoring Athletic Bilbao’s third goal.Photograph: Vincent West/ReutersIn Spain,Athletic BilbaothumpedAtlético Madrid3-0 on a miserable afternoon for Diego Simeone’s side. Nico Williams, Robert Navarro and Oihan Sancet’s goals gave the Basque hosts a resounding victory at San Mames.Athletic secured back-to-back wins under former Borussia Dortmund coach Edin Terzic, after losing their first two matches of the campaign.Julián Álvarez, who tried to leave Atlético to join Barcelona this summer, returned as a substitute after illness but the striker was ineffective in his second-half appearance.On SundayLa Ligaleaders Barcelona visit Valencia looking to move clear of Real Madrid, who lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.In the big game in the Eredivisie,Ajaxfell to a 3-1 home defeat byPSV. Ricardo Pepi had opened the scoring early on for the visitors, before Tolu Arokodare’s 23rd-minute leveller. Goals in stoppage time in either half, from Lutsharel Geertruida and Esmir Bajraktarevic respectively, then gave PSV the win.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballBundesligaBorussia Dortmund1899 HoffenheimBorussia MönchengladbachBayer LeverkusenSV ElversbergnewsShareReuse this content

title: Chilwell seals Crystal Palace comeback win after Mitchell double at Fulham | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Pierre Sage got his first win as Crystal Palace manager thanks to three goals from left wing-backs, leaving Fulham still without a league point under Álvaro Arbeloa
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Pierre Sage got his first win as Crystal Palace manager thanks to three goals from left wing-backs, leaving Fulham still without a league point under Álvaro Arbeloa
Content: Ben Chilwell began life back at Crystal Palace in memorable fashion with what proved to be the winning goal at Fulham.Photograph: Tony O Brien/ReutersView image in fullscreenBen Chilwell began life back at Crystal Palace in memorable fashion with what proved to be the winning goal at Fulham.Photograph: Tony O Brien/ReutersPremier LeagueChilwell seals Crystal Palace comeback win after Mitchell double at FulhamEd Aaronsat Craven CottageSat 5 Sep 2026 12.13 EDTLast modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 14.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe managers may have changed but the result stays the same. For the fourth successive trip to this part of west London, Crystal Palace returned over the river with a win as Pierre Sage got his reign off the mark in dramatic style. Their hero was Ben Chilwell, the former England left-back who wassigned on deadline day from Strasbourg– this time permanently, after a loan spell in which he helped Palace win the FA Cup – after he came off the bench to volley home the winner.Manchester City 1-0 Coventry, Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace and more: football clockwatch – as it happenedRead moreIt was a bitter blow for Fulham’s new manager Álvaro Arbeloa, who had seen his side lead twice through the impressive Josh King – who showed his potential in front of the watching England manager, Thomas Tuchel – and César Palacios before being pegged back twice by Tyrick Mitchell, the second in a moment of pure slapstick. Arbeloa and his side left the pitch to boos from some supporters and remain pointless after three matches. But having won here three times in 2025 under Oliver Glasner, this has been a happy hunting ground for Palace and Chilwell could not contain his delight as he celebrated with Sage and the travelling fans at the full-time whistle.“Today’s lesson was free because we won but we were inefficient in buildup during the first half,” said Sage, who maintained his record of never losing three games in a row as a manager. “It’s really a difficult period for me because I don’t like the mindset of the team and the club in this moment because [the transfer market] is always open. I like to know who I will work with.”View image in fullscreenTyrick Mitchell equalised twice for Palace.Photograph: Tony O Brien/ReutersFulham, who had almost 65% possession and racked up 25 shots in total, had looked more likely to end their winless start until Mitchell’s second goal swung the momentum decisively in Palace’s favour. They have nowconceded seven goalsin theirfirst three league matchesand Arbeloa – who was managing Real Madrid a few months ago – knows they must improve before next week’s game to face Liverpool at Anfield.“We lost a game that we didn’t deserve to lose. But in football you need to take your chances and they did that better than us,” he said. “We need to learn quickly because things can change when you concede a goal.”It didn’t take long for Alex Iwobi – the 30-year-old who has become only the fifth player inPremier Leaguehistory to play 100 or more games for three clubs – to start pulling the strings for Fulham in midfield alongside the new £30m signing from Southampton, Shea Charles.
